get_aggregate_metrics.description: The numbers across the top of a Plausible dashboard - unique visitors, visits, pageviews, bounce rate and average visit duration - for a period you choose. One number per metric, returned on 'totals' so a later step can read totals.visitors directly. Add filters to ask the same question about a slice of the traffic.
get_aggregate_metrics.name: get_aggregate_metrics

parameters.description: The site's domain exactly as it is registered in Plausible, such as 'example.com'. It is the name at the top of the site's dashboard. Pasting the full URL works too.
parameters.name: site_id

parameters.description: Which numbers to return. Leave blank for visitors, visits, pageviews, bounce_rate, visit_duration.
parameters.name: metrics

parameters.description: Which period to report on. Ignored when both dates below are set. Defaults to 7d.
parameters.name: date_range

parameters.description: The first day to include. Set this and 'To' together to use an exact range instead of the period above; leave both blank to use the period.
parameters.name: start_date

parameters.description: The last day to include. Has to be set together with 'From'.
parameters.name: end_date

parameters.description: Narrow the query, using Plausible's filter syntax: a list of [operator, dimension, values] triples, such as [["is", "visit:country", ["EE", "GB"]]]. The operators are is, is_not, contains, contains_not, matches, matches_not, and they can be nested inside and, or and not.
parameters.name: filters

parameters.description: Count data imported from Google Analytics or a CSV alongside what Plausible measured itself. Off by default, which is Plausible's own default. Check 'meta' on the result if the numbers look wrong - Plausible reports there when it had to skip an import.
parameters.name: include_imports

date_range.description: The period the query covered: either the shorthand that was used ('7d'), or the two dates it ran between.

meta.description: Plausible's own metadata for the query. Its keys are conditional: 'total_rows' and 'time_labels' only appear when they were asked for, and the 'imports_*' keys only on a site with imported data.

items.description: One row, with a key per metric and per dimension the step asked for - for example {'page': '/pricing', 'visitors': 412}. The 'metrics' and 'dimensions' fields on the result list those keys in order.

totals.description: One value per metric asked for, for the whole period - for example {'visitors': 1204, 'bounce_rate': 41}.

send_event.description: Record a pageview or a custom event against a site - a signup completing, an order being placed, anything that happens somewhere a tracking script cannot see. This is the one step here that works on every Plausible plan, because the events endpoint needs no API key. Two things to know: Plausible answers 'accepted' without promising to count it, so check 'dropped' on the result; and it works out who the visitor is from the User-Agent and IP address it is sent, so leaving both blank attributes every event to this server as one visitor.
send_event.name: send_event

parameters.description: The site's domain exactly as it is registered in Plausible, such as 'example.com'. It is the name at the top of the site's dashboard. Pasting the full URL works too.
parameters.name: site_id

parameters.description: What happened. Use the goal's exact name to record a conversion, or 'pageview' - the one reserved name - to record a page view. Defaults to 'pageview'.
parameters.name: name

parameters.description: The address of the page the event happened on. A path beginning with '/' is completed with the site's own domain.
parameters.name: url

parameters.description: Where the visitor came from, if you know it. Feeds the sources and channels breakdowns.
parameters.name: referrer

parameters.description: Extra fields to record with the event, which you can then break down by. At most 30 of them.
parameters.name: props

parameters.description: Money this event brought in, as {"currency": "USD", "amount": 15.99}. Only counted when the goal is set up as a revenue goal in Plausible.
parameters.name: revenue

parameters.description: Whether this event stops the visit counting as a bounce. Leave blank for Plausible's own default.
parameters.name: interactive

parameters.description: The visitor's User-Agent string. Plausible works out who the visitor is from this, so pass the real one through when you have it. Left blank, every event from this workflow looks like the same datacentre visitor and may be discarded as a bot.
parameters.name: user_agent

parameters.description: The visitor's IP address, used for the country, region and city breakdowns. Plausible hashes it and does not store it. Left blank, the event is located wherever this server is.
parameters.name: client_ip

description: Read a Plausible Analytics site from a workflow: totals, visitors over time, current visitors, and breakdowns by page, source, channel, campaign, country, device, browser and goal - and send events back in for things that happen where a tracking script cannot see them. Works with Plausible Cloud and with self-hosted Community Edition.
